title: Construction Work — Site Clearing and Ground Preparation
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. Site clearing and ground preparation is the first operation on any construction job. Work sequence: (1) survey and mark property boundaries and setbacks; (2) obtain permits and call utility locators to mark buried lines; (3) clear vegetation, brush, and trees, grubbing out stumps; (4) demolish and haul away any existing structures or slabs; (5) strip topsoil and stockpile it for final grading; (6) rough-grade the site to the elevations on the grading plan, cutting high spots and filling low spots; (7) compact the subgrade with a plate compactor or roller until it passes a proof-roll; (8) install erosion controls such as silt fence before excavation begins. Materials and equipment: survey stakes and flagging, chainsaw and brush cutter, excavator or skid-steer, dump trucks, fill dirt and gravel, silt fence. Safety: call 811 before digging, wear hard hats and hi-vis vests, keep machines clear of workers on foot, and never work under an unsupported excavation wall.
capabilities: Sequence the eight site-clearing steps in order
Estimate equipment needed for a given lot size
List erosion-control measures for the job
Verify subgrade compaction before the next trade

title: Construction Work — Excavation and Foundation Work
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. Excavation removes soil to the depth the foundation design requires; the foundation then transfers the building's load to stable ground. Sequence: (1) lay out the foundation lines with batter boards and string; (2) excavate to the design depth plus room for forms and drainage, benching or sloping walls deeper than 5 feet per safety rules; (3) install perimeter drain tile and gravel bed at the footing level; (4) build footing forms, set rebar per the structural plan, and pour concrete footings; (5) build foundation wall forms on the cured footings, set vertical and horizontal rebar, and pour the walls; (6) waterproof the exterior walls and install protection board; (7) backfill in 12-inch lifts, compacting each lift; (8) rough-grade away from the foundation for drainage. Materials: excavated soil or imported fill, footing concrete (typically 3000+ psi), rebar, form lumber or panels, drain tile, waterproofing membrane. Key check: the footing must sit below the local frost line, or frost heave will crack the foundation.
capabilities: Lay out foundation lines with batter boards
Compute excavation volume from plan dimensions
Verify rebar placement against a structural plan

title: Construction Work — Concrete Work and Curing
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. Good concrete work is about mix, placement, and cure. Steps: (1) confirm the mix design (strength, slump, aggregate size) with the supplier; (2) prep and wet the forms and subgrade; (3) place concrete starting at the far end, working back toward the truck or pump; (4) consolidate with a vibrator to remove air pockets, without over-vibrating and segregating the mix; (5) screed to grade and float the surface; (6) apply the finish — broom for exterior traction, trowel for smooth interior; (7) cut control joints within 24 hours, spaced about 24 to 30 times the slab thickness in inches; (8) cure: keep the concrete moist and above 50 F for at least 7 days (28 for full strength development). Materials: ready-mix concrete, forms, rebar or wire mesh, vibrator, screeds, floats, curing compound or wet burlap. Never add water to the truck on site beyond the allowed slump — it weakens the mix.
capabilities: Choose the right concrete mix for the job
Compute slab volume and order quantity

title: Construction Work — Framing: Wood and Steel
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. Framing is the building's skeleton. Wood framing sequence: (1) anchor the sill plate to the foundation with anchor bolts; (2) build and stand the exterior walls, plumbing and bracing them; (3) set floor joists or trusses and deck the subfloor; (4) stand interior walls; (5) set roof rafters or trusses, brace, and sheath; (6) install windows and doors, then house wrap. Steel framing follows the same skeleton logic with tracks, studs, and joists fastened by screws. Layout standards: wall studs and floor joists at 16 inches on center for load-bearing work; headers over every opening sized per span tables; sheathing nailed per the nailing schedule (typically 6 inches on edges, 12 in the field). Materials: pressure-treated sill lumber, studs, joists, trusses, sheathing, nails or structural screws, hurricane ties where required. Check: every wall must be plumb and every floor level before sheathing locks it in.
capabilities: Lay out wall framing at 16 inches on center
Sequence wall, floor, and roof framing
List the nailing schedule for sheathing
Verify plumb and level before sheathing

title: Construction Work — Roofing Installation
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. A roof fails at the details, not the shingles. Sequence: (1) inspect the deck — replace any soft or rotted sheathing; (2) install drip edge along eaves and rakes; (3) roll out underlayment from the eave upward, overlapping per manufacturer spec, with ice-and-water shield at eaves in cold climates; (4) install starter strip shingles along the eaves; (5) lay field shingles in courses, staggering joints and nailing per the wind zone (typically 4-6 nails per shingle); (6) flash every penetration — vents, chimneys, skylights — with step flashing and counter-flashing; (7) install ridge cap shingles; (8) clean up nails with a magnetic sweeper. Materials: shingles or panels, underlayment, ice-and-water shield, drip edge, flashing, roofing nails, ridge cap. Safety: fall protection is required on slopes — harness and anchor, or guardrails. Never roof in high wind.
capabilities: Sequence the roofing layers from deck to ridge
Compute shingle quantity from roof area
Verify nailing pattern for the wind zone

title: Construction Work — Electrical and Plumbing Rough-In
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. Rough-in installs the hidden systems before walls close. Electrical rough-in: (1) mount the panel and meter base; (2) run circuits per the electrical plan, drilling studs at center and protecting wires with nail plates; (3) set boxes for switches, outlets, and fixtures at standard heights; (4) pull wire, leaving slack at boxes; (5) ground everything and label every circuit. Plumbing rough-in: (1) set the main stack and branch drains with proper slope (1/4 inch per foot for drains under 3 inches); (2) install water supply lines, pressure-testing before concealment; (3) set tub and shower valves; (4) install venting so every trap is protected. Then both trades call for rough-in inspection — walls stay open until the inspector passes the work. Materials: NM cable or conduit, breaker panel, boxes, devices, PVC/ABS drain pipe, PEX or copper supply pipe, fittings, nail plates. Rule: never bury a joint or splice where it cannot be accessed.
capabilities: Check drain slope against code minimum
Verify nail-plate protection on bored studs

title: Construction Work — Interior Finishing
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. Finishing turns the framed shell into rooms. Sequence: (1) hang drywall, then tape, mud, and sand in three coats; (2) prime and paint ceilings then walls; (3) install interior doors, trim, and baseboards; (4) lay flooring — tile first in wet areas, then wood or carpet; (5) set cabinets and countertops; (6) install plumbing fixtures and electrical devices (the 'trim-out'); (7) install HVAC registers and grilles; (8) final paint touch-ups and a thorough cleanup. Materials: drywall, joint compound, paint, trim lumber, doors, flooring, cabinets, fixtures, devices. Order matters: paint before flooring to protect floors, cabinets before countertops, and trim-out last so finishes are not damaged by rough work. Check: hold drywall screws slightly below the surface without tearing the paper.

title: Construction Work — Final Inspection and Handover
body: Public edition. Public construction reference, fact-checked. Final inspection and handover close the job legally and cleanly. Sequence: (1) complete a punch list walkthrough, room by room, noting every defect; (2) correct all punch-list items and re-walk; (3) schedule the building final inspection — the inspector checks egress, smoke and CO alarms, handrails, GFCI protection, and that all permitted work matches the plans; (4) correct any inspection write-ups and obtain the certificate of occupancy; (5) compile the handover package: as-built drawings, equipment manuals, warranty documents, and spare materials (paint, tile, shingles); (6) demonstrate systems to the owner — HVAC, water shutoffs, breaker panel, irrigation; (7) hand over keys, codes, and the warranty schedule. Materials for the package: labeled binders or digital files with every manual and warranty. Rule: never hand over a building without written warranties and the location of every shutoff valve and breaker.
capabilities: Demonstrate home systems to the owner
